predecessors.name: Duchy of Pomerania
predecessors.text: the whole Duchy of Pomerania, Hither and Farther Pomerania, as the duchy-of-pomerania dossier draws it

successors.name: Kingdom of Prussia
successors.text: Western Pomerania north of the Peene, with Rügen, Stralsund and Greifswald

ledger.x: 6 July 1630: Gustavus Adolphus lands on Usedom and Swedish Pomerania begins.
1630: Sweden holds the duchy under the Treaty of Stettin.
10 March 1637: Bogislaw XIV dies, the last of his house, and the occupation of the duchy becomes Swedish administration.
1637-1638: the Swedes administer the whole duchy.
24/25 October 1637: imperial forces under von Bredow enter Western Pomerania.
24 October 1648: the Peace of Westphalia leaves Farther Pomerania to Brandenburg.
24 October 1648: Sweden receives Wismar.
4 May 1653: the Treaty of Stettin settles the border with Brandenburg 'in Sweden's favour'.
1675: Danish forces capture Wismar in the Scanian War.
1679: Wismar back under Sweden.
1679: Brandenburg keeps Gollnow and the strip east of the Oder as a pawn.
1693: reparations paid, the pawned strip returns to Sweden.
1715: Denmark occupies Swedish Pomerania.
21 January 1720: the Treaty of Stockholm gives Prussia southern Pomerania.
17 January 1721: Denmark returns the Pomeranian territories.
1803: Sweden cedes Wismar to Mecklenburg-Schwerin.
1807: French forces occupy Swedish Pomerania.
1810: 'Under the Treaty of Paris, signed in 1810, the territory was returned to Sweden.'
14 January 1814: the Treaty of Kiel cedes Pomerania to Denmark in exchange for Norway: 'Sweden ceded Pomerania to Denmark'.
23 October 1815: Swedish Pomerania passes to Prussia.

wars.name: Thirty Years War (Swedish phase)
wars.outcome: Sweden cleared Pomerania of imperial forces in 1631, held it against Brandenburg's inheritance claim after 1637 and kept Western Pomerania, Rügen, Usedom, Wolin and a strip of Farther Pomerania at the Peace of Westphalia (24 October 1648).

wars.name: Scanian War
wars.outcome: Denmark captured Wismar in 1675; at Saint-Germain-en-Laye (1679) Sweden was restored its Pomeranian territories except Gollnow and the strip east of the Oder, pawned to Brandenburg until 1693.

wars.name: Great Northern War
wars.outcome: Siege of Stralsund 1711-1715; Denmark occupied Swedish Pomerania 1715-1721; the Treaty of Stockholm (21 January 1720) gave Prussia the land south of the Peene, east of the Oder, Wolin and Usedom; Sweden kept the north.

certainty.note: The duchy's occupation and the Brandenburg claim were not fixed by a line until the Treaty of Stettin of 4 May 1653.
Treaty lines: Stettin 1653, Saint-Germain 1679 and Stockholm 1720 (the Peene).
